page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 504.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 7.88 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 2458 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark testing, the E64ds_v4 demonstrates strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 216.19 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 96.58 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers a strong result at 248.82 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and extended instructions tests show strong performance, reflecting its capability for data-heavy workloads. However, single-core CPU performance and large-model LLM text generation are relatively weaker, indicating a preference for parallelized, memory-bound tasks over raw single-threaded compute or heavy AI generation.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local SSD capacity, the E64ds_v4 offers high resource density for memory-intensive enterprise applications. The qualitative cost efficiency is favorable for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets combined with fast local scratch space. This makes the server highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics pipelines, and enterprise resource planning applications.
